findings.title: Extinction ratio is double-counted: full ER hit taken at launch (avg->OMA) AND again as ER penalty on OMA sensitivity
findings.claim: LinkBudget.sensitivity_oma_dbm adds er_penalty_db(ER) = 10log10((ER+1)/(ER-1)) to an OMA-domain sensitivity, but the launch side already charges the identical amount via _avg_to_oma_db, so every budget is pessimistic by exactly er_penalty_db (2.84 dB for the DR4 preset at ER=5 dB, 3.66 dB for the CPO preset at ER=4 dB).
findings.evidence: For a thermal-limited receiver with signal-independent noise and mid-eye thresholds, the required outer OMA is 2q(M-1)i_n/R, independent of ER; Agrawal's eq. 4.6.4 penalty (ER+1)/(ER-1) is precisely the conversion between average-power sensitivity and this fixed OMA (P_avg = OMA/2 * (ER+1)/(ER-1)), i.e. it applies only when the budget is carried in average power. Computed: at ER=5 dB the launch conversion _avg_to_oma_db docks 10log10(2)-10log10(2(ER-1)/(ER+1)) = 2.8442 dB vs infinite ER, and er_penalty_db(5.0) = 2.8442 dB is then added again on the sensitivity side — the same term to all digits. Net: launched OMA = P_top(1-1/ER) (physically exact, full ER effect included) yet required OMA is still inflated by (ER+1)/(ER-1). The docstring's framing as a 'conservative allocation' is not an independent effect; it is literally the same factor twice.
findings.suggested_fix: In sensitivity_oma_dbm (and the corresponding rows of report()), drop the er_penalty_db term; ER then enters the budget once, correctly, through _avg_to_oma_db at the transmitter. Alternatively, run the budget in average power and apply er_penalty_db to an average-power sensitivity — but not both. If a deliberate extra allocation for ER-related threshold offset is wanted, make it an explicit named entry in penalties_db, not the full Agrawal factor.

findings.title: energy_per_bit_pj laser_shared_by divides laser wall-plug energy by N while each lane still receives full per-line power
findings.claim: With laser_shared_by = N, the function models ceil(n_lanes/N) lasers each emitting only link.laser.power_dbm, while the LinkBudget simultaneously assumes every lane sees the full laser.power_dbm at the launch reference plane; a source feeding N lanes (split CW or N-line comb) must emit >= N x the per-line power, so laser energy per bit is silently underestimated by a factor of ~N.
findings.evidence: Counter-example (preset_cpo_optical_io, 6.5 dBm/line, wpe=0.10, 8 lanes, laser_shared_by=8): code returns laser = 0.174 pJ/bit, modeling the shared source at dbm_to_mw(6.5)/0.10 = 44.7 mW electrical; physically the source must supply 8 lines x 4.47 mW optical = 357 mW electrical, i.e. 1.40 pJ/bit — an 8x underestimate. Sharing a source amortizes control/TEC overhead, not the raw optical power per line; energy conservation forbids delivering power_dbm to N lanes from one power_dbm emitter. Note tests/test_link.py:211 asserts e_shared['laser'] == e['laser']/4, locking in the unphysical behavior — the test passes with broken physics.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the shared source emit laser_shared_by x the per-line power: laser_mw = n_lasers * laser_shared_by_effective_lines * dbm_to_mw(power_dbm) / wpe (equivalently just n_lanes * dbm_to_mw(power_dbm) / wpe), and let laser_shared_by amortize only a separate fixed per-device overhead term (or a wpe improvement). Fix tests/test_link.py:210-211 accordingly. If the current semantics ('power_dbm is the whole source, lanes tap a split of it') is intended instead, the LinkBudget launch power and this function must use consistent definitions and the split loss must appear in the path.

findings.title: expected_tuning_power_mw's heat-only justification is wrong: red-shift-only locking averages FSR/2, not FSR/4
findings.claim: The docstring claims that for heat-only red shift, redefining the target to the nearest resonance order red of the as-built resonance 'gives the same uniform [0, FSR/2] distribution'; in fact the red-ward distance to the target (mod FSR) is uniform on [0, FSR) with mean FSR/2, so for the physically common case (silicon heaters can only red-shift) the returned FSR/4-based power underestimates expected tuning power by 2x.
findings.evidence: With as-built offset u ~ U[0, FSR), bidirectional locking needs min(u, FSR-u) ~ U[0, FSR/2], mean FSR/4 (function's headline model — correct). Red-only locking needs (FSR - u) mod FSR ~ U[0, FSR), mean FSR/2. Monte-Carlo (1e6 samples): mean bidirectional shift = 0.2499 FSR, mean red-only shift = 0.4998 FSR. A per-ring uniform [0, FSR/2] red-only distribution is only achievable with bank-level channel reassignment (barrel shift), which changes the statistics to ~channel-spacing/2 per ring, not FSR/4 — neither matches the docstring's claim.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add a unidirectional flag (mean FSR/2 for heat-only, FSR/4 for bidirectional/pre-biased heaters) or correct the docstring to state that FSR/4 assumes bidirectional tuning (e.g. heater pre-bias) and that pure red-shift locking without channel reassignment averages FSR/2.

findings.title: Ring resonators use exp(+iφ) while all other components use exp(-iβL): conjugated phase breaks composition and gives negative group delay
findings.claim: RingAllPass and RingAddDrop build their transfer functions with round-trip factor a*exp(+1j*phi) (lines 351, 407-408), the opposite phase convention from Straight/MZI/PhaseShifter which use exp(-1j*2*pi*neff*L/wl). The ring S-parameters are therefore the complex conjugates of the physically correct ones in the library's own convention: transmission phase, group delay, and dispersion have the wrong sign, and any Circuit that interferes a ring with other components produces wrong power spectra. The module docstring's claim that 'magnitudes, resonance positions, and linewidths are identical in either sign convention' is only true for an isolated ring, not under the composability contract (ports/s_params for Circuit) that the module advertises.
findings.evidence: Built the identical physical all-pass ring (L=60um, neff0=2.4, ng=4.2, kappa=0.2, 0.1 dB/cm) from DirectionalCoupler+Straight closed through Circuit and compared with RingAllPass: |S21| agrees to 2.1e-15, but max phase mismatch is 6.23 rad while the mismatch against conj(RingAllPass) is 2.0e-12 — exact conjugation. Physical group delay -d(arg S21)/d(omega) at resonance: composed ring +15.08 ps (correct: enhanced, causal, ~F*T_rt/pi with bare round-trip 0.84 ps), analytic RingAllPass -15.08 ps (acausal advance for a low-loss over-coupled all-pass). Composing a ring-loaded MZI (RingAllPass in one arm vs the equivalent DC+Straight ring) changes the through-port spectrum by up to 0.48 dB in this example (worse for other reference-arm phases). Bogaerts 2012 writes e^{+iφ} under the e^{-iωt} physics convention; this library's Straight uses the engineering e^{-iβL} convention, so the ring formulas must be conjugated (a*exp(-1j*phi), and exp(-1j*phi/2) with a leading conjugated drop coefficient) to be consistent.
findings.suggested_fix: In RingAllPass._round_trip/s_params and RingAddDrop.s_params, use ae = a*exp(-1j*phi) and half = sqrt(a)*exp(-1j*phi/2) so through = (t - a e^{-iφ})/(1 - t a e^{-iφ}), drop = -sqrt(k1 k2) sqrt(a) e^{-iφ/2}/(1 - t1 t2 a e^{-iφ}); update the module docstring. Magnitudes, resonances, linewidths, and existing tests are unchanged; phases become consistent with Straight/MZI and with Circuit composition.

findings.title: Silicon Sellmeier resonance term transcribed as B*λ²/(λ²-λ₁²) instead of B*λ₁²/(λ²-λ₁²): n_si high by ~0.0012 everywhere
findings.claim: n_si computes n² = 11.6858 + 0.939816/λ² + 8.10461e-3*λ²/(λ² - 1.1071²), but the cited Li-1980-derived fit is n² = ε + A/λ² + B*λ₁²/(λ² - λ₁²) with λ₁ = 1.1071 um (as quoted e.g. in Frey, Leviton & Madison 2006). Using λ² in the numerator is algebraically identical to adding the constant B = 8.10461e-3 to n², so n is biased high by +0.00116 to +0.00119 over the whole 1.2-14 um range.
findings.evidence: Identity: Bλ²/(λ²-λ₁²) = B + Bλ₁²/(λ²-λ₁²); computed n² offset is exactly 8.10461e-3 at all wavelengths. Code vs reference form: n(1.31)=3.501686 vs 3.500529; n(1.55)=3.477575 vs 3.476410; n(10.6)=3.420871 vs 3.419686. The function's own docstring states n(1.55) ≈ 3.476, which matches the reference form (3.4764), not the code (3.4776). Dispersion and group index are unaffected (constant n² offset; ng_si(1.55)=3.595 is fine), but the neff bias propagates ~1:1 through the EIM solver and shifts e.g. a simulated ring resonance by ~λ·Δn/ng ≈ 0.4 nm at 1.55 um.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the third term with 8.10461e-3 * 1.1071**2 / (wl2 - 1.1071**2) (equivalently subtract the constant 8.10461e-3 from 11.6858 while keeping the current form).

findings.title: Ring models use conjugated phase convention; composing them in Circuit with other components gives wrong spectra
findings.claim: RingAllPass and RingAddDrop use exp(+1j*phi) round-trip phase while every other component (Straight, PhaseShifter, MZI) uses exp(-1j*beta*L), so the analytic ring response is the complex conjugate of the physically composed one; the module docstring's assurance that 'magnitudes, resonance positions, and linewidths are identical in either sign convention' is false as soon as a ring is placed in any multipath circuit, and Circuit silently combines the two conventions.
findings.evidence: Computed: a RingAllPass (L=100 um, kappa=0.1, 0.5 dB/cm) vs the identical ring built from DirectionalCoupler+Straight in Circuit gives t_analytic = conj(t_circuit) to 4e-12 (magnitudes equal to 2e-13, phase slope at resonance +39758 vs -39758 rad/um, i.e. group-delay sign flipped / anti-causal). Embedding each in one arm of a Circuit-built MZI with a pi/2 reference arm: analytic-ring MZI has its transmission null at 1548.98 nm, the coupler-built (physically consistent) MZI at 1549.08 nm — ~100 pm apart, with up to 45.2 dB disagreement at a fixed wavelength (-45.2 dB vs -0.05 dB). No test pins ring phase inside Circuit (tests check only magnitudes/unitarity), so this passes the suite.
findings.suggested_fix: Change RingAllPass/RingAddDrop to the delay convention used everywhere else: ae = a*exp(-1j*phi) and half-ring factor sqrt(a)*exp(-1j*phi/2) (i.e. through = (t - a e^{-i phi})/(1 - t a e^{-i phi}), drop = -sqrt(k1 k2) sqrt(a) e^{-i phi/2}/D). Magnitude spectra and all existing tests are unchanged; add a regression test comparing RingAllPass phase against a DirectionalCoupler+Straight feedback loop solved by Circuit. Also correct the module-docstring claim that the sign convention cannot matter.

findings.title: MonteCarloResult.sensitivity() silently returns 0.0 for every parameter whenever any corner failed
findings.claim: sensitivity() computes Pearson r with m = self.samples without masking NaN, so a single failed corner (run() deliberately records metric ValueError as NaN, e.g. an unreachable-RIN corner) makes m.mean() and the denominator NaN; the guard 'denom > 0' is False for NaN and every parameter gets 0.0 — the advertised 'sensitivity ranking' / 'dominant-variation ranking' silently degenerates to all-zeros with no warning, and report() prints the meaningless ranking.
findings.evidence: Computed counter-example: metric(p) = 3*a + b raising ValueError when a > 2 (Normal a: mean 0 sigma 1; Uniform b: [-0.1, 0.1]), n = 2000, seed 1 -> n_failed = 52, sensitivity() = {'a': 0.0, 'b': 0.0} and report() ends with 'sensitivity (Pearson r): a +0.00, b +0.00', whereas the true correlation for a is ~ +1.0. With zero failed corners the same setup returns r_a ~ 0.999, confirming the NaN contamination is the cause.
findings.suggested_fix: Mask failed corners before correlating: ok = ~np.isnan(self.samples); m = self.samples[ok]; x = x[ok] for each parameter (and return 0.0 / raise only if fewer than 2 valid samples). Add a test asserting sensitivity() still ranks parameters correctly when some corners raise.
